summary: A floor-based hip opener with one shin forward and the other leg extended behind, stretching the outer hip of the front leg and the front of the back hip.
steps: Start on hands and knees, then slide one knee forward behind its wrist with the shin angled across your body.
Extend the other leg straight back, resting the top of the foot on the floor.
Square your hips toward the floor and support your weight on your hands or forearms.
Lean forward gently until you feel a stretch in the front-leg hip and the back-leg thigh, staying pain-free.
Hold 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily, then switch sides.

summary: A static inverted-V support on hands and feet that builds shoulder strength and overhead pushing position for pike push-ups.
steps: Start in a plank with hands about shoulder-width apart and feet hip-width apart.
Walk your feet in and lift your hips high so your body forms an inverted V.
Straighten your elbows and push the floor away so your shoulders stay active and your head sits between your arms.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.
mistakes: Bending the elbows or letting the head drop toward the floor
Rounding the back instead of lifting the hips

summary: A plank held while slowly reaching one arm forward at a time, challenging the core to resist rotation and keeping the shoulders stable.
steps: Set up in a high plank with hands under your shoulders and feet hip-width apart, eyes on the floor.
Brace your core and glutes so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Slowly reach one arm straight forward, then return the hand to the floor.
Alternate arms for the set time, keeping your hips as still as possible.
mistakes: Hips rotating or shifting toward the support arm
Lower back sagging during the reach

summary: A high or forearm plank with alternating leg lifts that trains the glutes while the core resists sagging and rotation.
steps: Set up in a plank on your hands or forearms with your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Lift one foot a few inches off the floor, keeping the leg straight, then lower it with control.
Alternate legs for the set time without letting your hips move.
mistakes: Arching the lower back to lift the leg higher
Hips tilting or rotating as the leg lifts

summary: A plank that moves between forearms and hands, training the triceps, shoulders, and core to keep the body stable throughout.
steps: Start in a forearm plank with elbows under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
Place one hand on the floor under its shoulder and press up, then bring the other hand up into a high plank.
Lower back down one forearm at a time to the forearm plank.
Keep alternating the leading arm for the set time, holding a steady plank throughout.
mistakes: Hips swaying side to side as you change levels
Hands landing too far forward of the shoulders

summary: A lying core drill that tilts the pelvis to flatten the lower back, teaching abdominal and glute control of pelvic position.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, arms relaxed by your sides.
Gently tighten your lower abs and glutes to tilt your pelvis back and press your lower back into the floor.
Keep your upper body relaxed and breathe normally.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, then release.
mistakes: Lifting the hips off the floor
Pushing with the feet instead of using the abs

summary: A bodyweight squat with hands behind the head that strengthens the legs and glutes while training an upright torso.
steps: Stand with feet about hip-width apart, toes forward, and fingers lightly laced behind your head with elbows out.
Push your hips back and bend your knees, keeping your chest up and back straight.
Lower as deep as you can control, pressing your knees out in line with your toes.
Drive through your whole foot to stand back up tall.
mistakes: Elbows collapsing forward and pulling on the neck

summary: A face-down shoulder blade drill that lifts the arms from the sides to strengthen the middle and lower trapezius.
steps: Lie face down with your forehead on a folded towel and arms resting at your sides, palms facing in.
Draw your shoulder blades back and down toward your spine.
Lift your arms a few inches off the floor while keeping the neck long.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower your arms with control.
mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears
Lifting the head or arching the lower back
Swinging the arms up without moving the shoulder blades

summary: A static hold at a chosen height of the pull-up, building pulling strength in the lats, upper back, and biceps.
steps: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip about shoulder-width apart.
Pull your shoulder blades down and pull yourself up to the height you want to train, such as elbows at a right angle.
Keep your chest up, legs together, and body still.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, then lower with control.
mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears
Slowly sinking instead of holding the height

summary: A static hold with the chin above the bar that strengthens the hardest top range of the pull-up in the lats and biceps.
steps: Stand on a box or bench under a pull-up bar and grip it overhand about shoulder-width apart.
Step up so your chin is above the bar with elbows fully bent and shoulders pulled down.
Take your feet off the box and keep your chest up toward the bar.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, then step back onto the box or lower with control.
mistakes: Craning the neck to keep the chin up

summary: A push-up followed by a rotation into a side plank, training the chest and triceps along with shoulder stability and the obliques.
steps: Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
Lower your chest toward the floor, then press back up.
Rotate your body to one side into a side plank, reaching the top arm toward the ceiling.
Return to the plank and repeat, rotating to the other side.
mistakes: Hips sagging during the push-up or rotation
Rotating the shoulders before the hips
Bottom hand placed far from the shoulder

summary: A seated or lying drill that tightens the thigh muscle with the leg straight, rebuilding quadriceps activation and control.
steps: Sit or lie with your legs straight, a small rolled towel under one knee if you like.
Tighten the front of your thigh to press the back of the knee down, so the kneecap draws upward.
Hold the contraction briefly without lifting the leg.
Relax the muscle fully, then repeat, and switch sides.
mistakes: Tensing the glutes or other muscles instead of the thigh

summary: A standing stretch for the front of the thigh that eases the quadriceps and hip flexors by drawing the heel toward the buttocks.
steps: Stand tall on one leg, holding a wall or chair for balance if needed.
Bend the other knee and hold that ankle with your hand.
Gently pull your heel toward your buttocks, keeping your knees close together.
Tuck your pelvis slightly forward until you feel a stretch in the front of the thigh, avoiding an arched back.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A lying ab exercise that curls the torso up while reaching the arms toward the ceiling, strengthening the abdominal muscles.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, and arms extended toward the ceiling.
Tighten your abs and curl your head and shoulders off the floor, reaching your hands as high as possible.
Pause briefly at the top without jerking.
Lower your upper back slowly to the floor.
mistakes: Jerking up with the arms or neck
Lower back arching off the floor

summary: A kneeling stretch with the back foot raised behind you that targets the hip flexors and front of the thigh.
steps: Kneel facing away from a bench or sofa and rest the top of your back foot on it, with the other foot flat in front.
Stack your torso upright over the back knee, with a pad under it for comfort.
Tuck your pelvis and squeeze the glute of the back leg.
Shift your hips gently forward until you feel a stretch in the front of the back hip and thigh.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.
mistakes: Arching the lower back to go deeper

summary: A side-lying hip rotation that lifts the top foot while the knees stay together, strengthening the glutes and hip rotators.
steps: Lie on your side with hips and knees bent and knees and feet stacked.
Rest your head on your lower arm and keep your pelvis still.
Keep your knees touching and lift your top foot upward by rotating at the hip.
Lower the foot back down slowly, then switch sides after the set.
mistakes: Rolling the pelvis back to lift the foot higher

summary: A face-down hip extension over a bench edge that lifts the legs behind you, strengthening the glutes and hamstrings.
steps: Lie face down on a sturdy bench or table with your hips at the edge and legs hanging toward the floor.
Hold the sides of the bench and keep your torso flat.
Squeeze your glutes and lift your straight legs until they are in line with your body.
Lower your legs slowly back down without letting them swing.
mistakes: Over-arching the lower back at the top
Bending the knees to finish the lift

summary: A kneeling lean-back that loads the quadriceps through a long range, strengthening the front of the thighs without equipment.
steps: Kneel on a padded surface with knees hip-width apart, shins on the floor, and torso upright.
Squeeze your glutes so your body forms a straight line from knees to head.
Lean back slowly, keeping hips extended, as far as you can control.
Pull yourself back to upright using your thighs.
mistakes: Bending at the hips instead of leaning as one unit
Leaning back further than you can return from

summary: A face-up plank on hands and heels that strengthens the core, glutes, and back of the body while opening the front of the shoulders.
steps: Sit with legs straight and hands on the floor slightly behind your hips, fingers pointing toward your feet.
Press through your hands and heels to lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to heels.
Squeeze your glutes and keep your chest open and neck neutral.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.

summary: A low-to-high diagonal pull with a band that trains rotational power through the core, hips, and shoulders.
steps: Anchor a resistance band below knee height and stand side-on to it with knees softly bent.
Hold the band with both hands near the hip closest to the anchor.
Rotate your hips and pull the band diagonally up and across your body to above the opposite shoulder.
Return slowly along the same path, then switch sides after the set.
mistakes: Rounding the back at the low position

summary: A seated or standing neck stretch that eases the right side of the upper neck and the muscle that lifts the shoulder blade.
steps: Sit or stand tall and let your right arm hang or rest the right hand behind your back.
Turn your head about halfway to the left and nod your chin toward your left armpit.
Place your left hand on the back of your head and add gentle pressure until you feel a stretch on the right side of the neck.
Hold 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily, then release slowly.

summary: A gentle side-bend of the neck that stretches the right side of the neck and upper trapezius.
steps: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Tilt your left ear toward your left shoulder without turning your head.
Rest your left hand on the right side of your head and add light pressure to deepen the stretch.
Keep the right shoulder down and hold 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily.

summary: A standing spinal roll that moves one vertebra at a time toward the floor, mobilizing the back and stretching the hamstrings.
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and knees soft.
Tuck your chin and slowly roll your upper body forward, one section of the spine at a time.
Let your arms hang and go as far as is comfortable, toward or onto the floor.
Roll back up just as slowly, stacking your spine until you stand tall.
mistakes: Hinging with a flat back instead of rolling

summary: A rolling sequence that flows from shoulders to a wide seated V, building core control and stretching the hamstrings and inner thighs.
steps: Sit with legs together and straight, then roll back onto your upper back, bringing your legs overhead.
Open your legs wide as they pass overhead.
Roll forward with control, using your abs to come up into a wide-legged seated V.
Reach your hands forward between your legs, then roll back again for the next rep.
cues: Legs wide on the way up
mistakes: Throwing the head to generate momentum
Collapsing the chest at the bottom of the reach

summary: A leaning row on suspension straps or rings that strengthens the back, rear shoulders, and biceps with adjustable bodyweight.
steps: Hold a handle in each hand, face the anchor, and walk your feet forward until you lean back with arms straight.
Brace your core and glutes so your body is straight from head to heels.
Pull your chest toward your hands, squeezing your shoulder blades together and keeping elbows close.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are straight.
mistakes: Dropping fast on the way down

summary: A deep low-lunge stretch that opens the hip flexors of the back leg and the groin and hamstring of the front leg.
steps: Step one foot forward into a long lunge and lower the back knee to the floor or keep it lifted.
Place both hands on the floor inside the front foot.
Sink your hips forward and down until you feel a stretch in the front of the back hip.
Keep your chest long and hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: An advanced push-up that lowers onto the forearms and presses back up, demanding strong triceps, chest, and shoulder control.
steps: Start in a high plank with hands slightly wider than shoulders and your body straight.
Lower your chest toward the floor, then shift back to set your forearms down on the floor.
Shift your weight forward over your hands and press off the forearms back to the bottom of a push-up.
Press through your palms to straighten your arms and return to the plank.
mistakes: Hips sagging or piking as you change levels
Dropping onto the forearms without control

summary: A face-down rotational leg swing from the push-up position that mobilizes the hips and spine while the shoulders hold steady.
steps: Start in a high plank with shoulders over hands and feet hip-width apart.
Bend one knee and lift that leg behind you, foot toward the ceiling.
Rotate your hips to swing the foot across your body toward the floor on the opposite side.
Reverse the movement back to the plank, then switch sides.
mistakes: Hands lifting or shifting off the floor

summary: A seated ab exercise that draws the knees in and across the body to each side, training the lower abs and obliques.
steps: Sit with hands on the floor behind you and lean back slightly with feet lifted.
Bring your knees in toward your chest and across toward one shoulder.
Extend your legs back out without letting your feet touch the floor.
Repeat toward the other side, alternating.
mistakes: Dropping the feet to rest between reps

summary: A seated cross-legged hip stretch that eases the glutes and outer hip with gentle, controlled pressure on the knee.
steps: Sit tall on a bench or chair with both feet flat on the floor.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee, letting the raised knee fall out to the side.
Keep your back straight and gently press the raised knee down until you feel a stretch in the outer hip.
Ease off and repeat the gentle press, then switch sides.

summary: A seated outward knee press that strengthens the glutes and outer hips.
steps: Sit tall on a chair or bench with feet flat, knees together, and a light band above your knees if you have one.
Hold the seat edges and brace your core gently.
Push your knees outward from the hips, pausing briefly at the widest point.
Return your knees together slowly, keeping tension throughout.
mistakes: Leaning the torso to help the knees move
Letting the knees snap back together
Lifting the feet off the floor

summary: A gentle seated stretch that eases the knee into full straightening, targeting the back of the knee and hamstrings.
steps: Sit with one leg straight in front of you and the heel propped on a low surface so the knee is unsupported.
Place both hands on the thigh just above the kneecap and keep the leg relaxed.
Gently press down toward the floor until you feel a stretch behind the knee.
Hold briefly, release, and repeat, then switch sides.
mistakes: Tensing the thigh against your hands

summary: A seated ab exercise that pulls the knees toward the chest and extends the legs, strengthening the lower abs and hip flexors.
steps: Sit on the floor with hands slightly behind your hips and lean back a little.
Lift your feet off the floor with knees bent.
Extend your legs out long, keeping them off the floor.
Pull your knees back toward your chest while bringing your chest toward them.
mistakes: Rounding the back and collapsing the chest
Letting the feet drop to the floor

summary: A wide-legged seated hinge with hands behind the head, moved down and up for reps to loosen the hamstrings, inner thighs and lower back.
steps: Sit with your legs straight and spread wide in a straddle.
Place your hands on the back of your head.
Hinge from the hips to bring your chest toward the floor, keeping the back long.
Sit back up tall and repeat.
mistakes: Rounding the upper back to go lower
Pulling on the neck with the hands

summary: A seated stretch that pulls one knee across the body to target the deep glute muscles and outer hip.
steps: Sit tall on the floor with one leg straight in front of you.
Cross the other foot over the straight leg and plant it outside the knee.
Hug the bent knee with the opposite arm and draw it gently toward the opposite shoulder.
Keep your spine tall and hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A seated stretch with the hands behind you that opens the front of the shoulders and chest by sliding the hips forward.
steps: Sit on the floor with your hands behind you, shoulder-width apart, fingers pointing back.
Straighten your elbows and lift your chest.
Slide your hips and feet forward so your shoulders lower toward the floor.
Stop at a comfortable stretch across the front of the shoulders and hold 20–30 seconds.

summary: A wall-supported forearm slide held near the top that stretches and engages the serratus and shoulder muscles.
steps: Stand facing a wall with forearms vertical against it, elbows and wrists touching.
Angle your arms slightly outward and push your forearms into the wall to spread your shoulder blades.
Slide your forearms up the wall until your elbows are about level with your chin.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, then slide back down.
mistakes: Arching the lower back to slide higher
Losing forearm contact with the wall

summary: A seated 90/90 hip position that stretches the hip rotators of both legs, with emphasis on internal rotation of the back hip.
steps: Sit with one leg in front, bent about 90 degrees, and the other leg to the side and behind, also bent about 90 degrees.
Keep both knees and shins on the floor and sit tall.
Keep your hips square and gently lean your torso forward over the front shin.
Hold 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily, then switch sides.
mistakes: Rounding the back to lean further
Lifting the back knee off the floor

summary: A standing wall stretch that lowers the chest between raised arms, stretching the lats and the shoulders into overhead reach.
steps: Place both hands on a wall above shoulder height, about shoulder-width apart.
Step back until your arms are straight and hinge at the hips.
Let your chest sink gently toward the floor while your arms reach overhead.
Keep your ribs down and hold 20–30 seconds.
mistakes: Arching the lower back to fake shoulder range

summary: A standing shoulder lift that strengthens the upper trapezius by raising and lowering the shoulders.
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and arms hanging straight at your sides.
Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as you can.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower your shoulders slowly back down.

summary: A push-up performed with one foot lifted that strengthens the chest and triceps while increasing core and hip stability demands.
steps: Set up in a high plank with shoulders over hands and feet hip-width apart.
Brace your core and lift one foot just off the floor, keeping your hips level.
Lower your chest toward the floor, keeping your body in a straight line.
Press back up, then switch the lifted foot for the next set.
mistakes: Hips twisting toward the lifted leg

summary: A side-lying crunch that lifts the shoulders toward the hip, strengthening the obliques.
steps: Lie on one side with knees bent and stacked, and the top hand lightly behind your head.
Rest the lower arm across your stomach or on the floor in front.
Squeeze the side of your waist to lift your shoulders off the floor toward your top hip.
Lower slowly, then switch sides after the set.
mistakes: Pulling on the head with the hand

summary: A side-lying leg raise that strengthens the outer hip and glutes while keeping the pelvis stacked and still.
steps: Lie on your side with the bottom leg bent for support and the top leg straight in line with your body.
Stack your hips and point the top toes forward.
Lift the top leg toward the ceiling, leading with the heel, without rolling back.
Lower the leg slowly, then switch sides after the set.
mistakes: Swinging the leg forward of the body
Lifting too high and hiking the hip

summary: A low lateral shuffle combined with a turn and squat that builds leg endurance, footwork, and conditioning.
steps: Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width in a low athletic stance.
Shuffle sideways three steps, pushing off the trailing leg without crossing your feet.
Pivot 180 degrees on the outside foot and drop into a squat.
Stand and shuffle back the other way, continuing the pattern.
mistakes: Knees caving in during the squat

summary: A wide-stance lateral squat that shifts the weight into one bent leg, strengthening the quadriceps and glutes.
steps: Stand tall with feet wide, a little more than shoulder-width apart, toes forward or slightly out.
Shift your hips back and to one side, bending that knee while the other leg stays straight.
Lower until the bent thigh is about parallel to the floor, knee in line with the foot.
Push through the bent leg back to the center, then alternate sides.
mistakes: Rounding the back to reach depth

summary: A standing overhead side bend that stretches the lats and the muscles along the side of the trunk.
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Raise one arm overhead and rest the other hand on your hip.
Reach up and over to the opposite side, bending at the waist without leaning forward or back.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A push-up that shifts the bodyweight over one hand at a time, loading each side of the chest, shoulders, and triceps more.
steps: Set up in a high plank with hands slightly wider than shoulders.
Shift your bodyweight toward one hand.
Lower your chest toward that hand, keeping your body straight, then press back up.
Return to center and repeat toward the other side.
mistakes: Hips sagging or twisting during the shift
Shifting only the head and chest, not the body

summary: A seated stretch over one straight leg that lengthens the hamstrings while the other leg rests folded inward.
steps: Sit with one leg straight in front, toes pointing up, and the other sole resting against the inner thigh.
Sit up tall with your chest open.
Exhale and hinge forward from the hips over the straight leg, keeping your back long.
Reach for your shin, ankle, or foot and hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A one-leg balance with eyes closed that trains ankle, knee, and hip stability without visual feedback.
steps: Stand within reach of a wall, counter, or chair.
Shift onto one leg with the knee slightly bent and lift the other foot clear of the floor.
Once steady, close your eyes and keep your hips level.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, then switch legs.
cues: Grip the floor with the foot
mistakes: Letting the hip of the free leg drop

summary: A lying single-leg bridge with a sliding heel curl that strengthens the hamstrings and glutes.
steps: Lie on your back with one heel on a towel or slider on a smooth floor and the other leg lifted.
Press into the heel and lift your hips into a bridge.
Keeping your hips high, slide the heel out until the leg is nearly straight.
Pull the heel back toward your hips, then lower and switch sides after the set.
mistakes: Hips dropping as the leg extends

summary: A single-leg press with the body turned sideways that targets the glutes and outer hip while also working the thighs.
steps: Sit in a leg press machine and rotate onto one hip.
Place one foot high on the platform with toes angled slightly outward.
Lower the platform with control, keeping the knee in line with the foot.
Press through the heel to extend the leg without locking the knee, then switch sides.
mistakes: Lifting the hips off the seat at the bottom
Locking the knee at the top

summary: A single-leg landing drill from a low step that trains soft, stable landings and balance through the leg muscles.
steps: Stand on a low, stable box or step.
Step off with one foot, without jumping.
Land softly on that foot, bending the hip, knee, and ankle to absorb the landing.
Hold the landing steady, then step back up and switch legs.
mistakes: Wobbling without settling into the hold

summary: A seated forward reach over straight legs that stretches the hamstrings and lower back.
steps: Sit on the floor with your legs straight in front of you, toes pointing up.
Sit up tall and reach both arms forward.
Hinge from the hips and reach toward or past your toes as far as is comfortable.
Hold 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily.

summary: A sit-up finished with a cross-body elbow drive that trains the abs and obliques with a quick rotation.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, and hands by your ears.
Sit up with control.
At the top, drive one elbow across your body toward the opposite side, then return to center.
Lower yourself back down with control, then alternate sides.
mistakes: Yanking the neck with the hands

summary: A seated calf stretch that draws the toes toward the shin, gently lengthening the calf muscles.
steps: Sit on the floor with one leg straight and the other bent comfortably.
Reach for the ball of the straight leg's foot, or loop a towel around it.
Gently pull your toes toward your shin until you feel a stretch in the calf.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A face-down back extension with arms out in a T that strengthens the upper back, rear shoulders, and spinal extensors.
steps: Lie face down with legs apart and arms out to the sides in a T, palms on the floor.
Lift your chest, arms, and legs off the floor, turning your thumbs toward the ceiling.
Pull your shoulder blades together and keep your neck long.
Bring your legs together and apart while holding the lift, then lower everything with control.
mistakes: Letting the arms drop below shoulder height

summary: A side-lying stretch for the back of the shoulder that gently rotates the forearm toward the floor.
steps: Lie on one side with the bottom arm out in front at shoulder height and the elbow bent to 90 degrees.
Settle some weight onto the bottom shoulder blade to keep it still.
Use the top hand to gently press the bottom forearm toward the floor.
Stop at a mild stretch at the back of the shoulder and hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A slow lowering from the top of a pull-up that builds the lat and biceps strength needed for full pull-ups.
steps: Stand on a box under a pull-up bar and grip it overhand about shoulder-width apart.
Step up so your chin is above the bar with elbows fully bent and shoulders down.
Take your feet off the box and lower yourself as slowly as you can until your arms are straight.
Step back onto the box to return to the top for the next rep.
mistakes: Dropping quickly through the bottom half
Jumping up instead of stepping to the top
Relaxing the shoulders at the bottom

summary: A bodyweight squat with a slow descent and a brief pause at the bottom that builds leg strength and control.
steps: Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
Sit your hips back and down, taking about three seconds to lower.
Pause briefly at the bottom, keeping your chest up.
Stand back up at a normal pace, pressing through your whole foot.

summary: A quick drop from tall to an athletic landing position that trains the legs and hips to absorb force.
steps: Stand tall on the balls of your feet with arms reaching overhead.
Do a small hop or snap down, swinging your arms down and back.
Land softly on both feet, bending your knees and hinging at the hips into an athletic stance.
Hold the landing briefly, then stand tall to reset.

summary: A half-kneeling stretch that opens the front of the hip and thigh of the back leg using a pelvic tuck.
steps: Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat in front, both knees bent about 90 degrees.
Stand your torso tall and tuck your pelvis under.
Squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg and shift your hips slightly forward.
Hold 20–30 seconds when you feel the stretch in the front of the back hip, then switch sides.

summary: A face-down forearm prop that gently extends the spine and stretches the abdominals and front of the trunk.
steps: Lie on your stomach with legs extended and the tops of your feet on the floor.
Place your forearms on the floor with elbows directly under your shoulders.
Press into your forearms to lift your chest, drawing your shoulder blades back and down.
Keep your lower back and glutes relaxed and hold 20–30 seconds.

summary: A deep squat held with an upward rotating arm reach that stretches the hips and opens the chest and upper back.
steps: Drop into a deep squat with feet flat and chest up.
Hold one ankle with the opposite hand and fold the other arm across your chest.
Rotate your chest open and reach the free arm toward the ceiling.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, then return to center and switch sides.

summary: A standing wall stretch with the back leg straight that targets the upper calf muscle.
steps: Stand facing a wall with your hands on it at chest height.
Step one foot back, keeping the back leg straight and the heel down.
Bend the front knee and lean your hips toward the wall until you feel a stretch in the back calf.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A standing cross-leg side lean that stretches the outer hip and thigh.
steps: Stand tall and cross one leg behind the other.
Raise the arm on the side of the back leg overhead.
Push your hip out to that side and lean your upper body gently the other way.
Hold 20–30 seconds when you feel the stretch along the outer hip, then switch sides.

summary: A wide-legged standing forward hinge that stretches the hamstrings and inner thighs.
steps: Stand with your feet as wide as is comfortable, toes forward.
Place your hands on your thighs or hips.
Push your hips back and hinge forward, keeping your back straight.
Let your hands lower toward the floor and hold the position, breathing steadily.
mistakes: Rounding the back to reach the floor

summary: A wide-stance standing hinge with hands behind the head, moved down and up for reps to loosen the hamstrings and inner thighs.
steps: Stand with feet wider than shoulder width, toes turned slightly out.
Place your hands on the back of your head.
Hinge at the hips and lower your chest toward the floor, keeping the back straight.
Stand back up by driving the hips forward, then repeat.
mistakes: Rounding the back to go lower
Pulling the head forward with the hands

summary: A standing side bend that draws the elbow toward the hip, strengthening the obliques and improving balance.
steps: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and hands lightly behind your head.
Bend your torso to one side, bringing your elbow toward your hip.
Squeeze the side of your waist at the bottom of the bend.
Return to upright and repeat on the other side.

summary: A standing wall stretch with the back knee bent that targets the soleus, the lower calf muscle.
steps: Stand facing a wall or chair with your hands on it for support.
Step one foot back a short distance with the heel down.
Bend both knees and sink your hips straight down until you feel a stretch low in the back calf.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A step-edge calf stretch that lets the heels drop below the step, stretching the calf muscles.
steps: Stand on a step with the balls of your feet on the edge and hold a rail or wall for balance.
Slowly lower one or both heels below the step until you feel a stretch in the calf.
Keep the knee straight for the upper calf, or bend it slightly for the lower calf.
Hold 20–30 seconds without bouncing, then switch sides if stretching one leg.

summary: A low-impact jumping jack that steps out to each side with an overhead arm swing, raising the heart rate and warming the body.
steps: Stand tall with feet together and arms at your sides.
Step one foot out to the side while swinging both arms overhead.
Bring the foot back to center and lower your arms.
Repeat to the other side, alternating at a steady, rhythmic pace.

summary: An advanced support hold with the legs straight and wide, demanding strong core compression, shoulder depression, and hip flexors.
steps: Sit with your legs straight and spread wide, hands on the floor or parallettes between your thighs.
Lock your arms and push down to lift your hips and legs off the floor.
Keep your legs straight and roughly horizontal, with shoulders pressed down.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.
mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears
Bending the knees to clear the floor

summary: A lying stretch that draws one straight leg toward the chest, lengthening the hamstrings and calf.
steps: Lie on your back with both legs extended.
Raise one leg and hold it with both hands behind the thigh.
Gently draw the leg toward you, keeping the knee as straight as possible and the lower back on the floor.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch legs.

summary: A calf stretch with your hands on a chair or wall for support that lengthens the calf of the back leg.
steps: Stand facing a sturdy chair back or wall and place your hands on it.
Step one foot back into a staggered stance, heel down and toes forward.
Lean your weight forward over the front leg until you feel a stretch in the back calf.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A split squat with a hand on a support for balance that builds the quadriceps and glutes one leg at a time.
steps: Stand in a split stance, one foot a stride in front of the other, with a hand on a wall, rack or chair back.
Lower your hips straight down by bending both knees until the back knee is just above the floor.
Keep your torso upright and your front heel down.
Push through the front foot to stand back up, using the support only for balance.
Finish your reps, then switch sides.
mistakes: Pulling on the support to hold yourself up

summary: A suspension chest fly that brings the arms together to cross in front, strengthening the chest and shoulders.
steps: Hold a handle in each hand facing away from the anchor and lean forward with arms extended at chest height.
Brace your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Open your arms wide with a slight elbow bend, letting your body lower forward.
Squeeze your chest to bring the arms back together, crossing the hands slightly in front of you.
mistakes: Bending the elbows into a press

summary: A lying core exercise that lowers one foot at a time to tap the floor, training the deep abdominals to keep the lower back steady.
steps: Lie on your back with arms by your sides and legs in tabletop, knees bent to 90 degrees.
Brace your core and press your lower back gently into the floor.
Lower one foot slowly to tap the floor, keeping the knee bend the same.
Return the leg to tabletop and alternate sides.
mistakes: Lower back arching off the floor

summary: A standing hinge that reaches toward the toes, stretching the hamstrings and calves while warming up the hips.
steps: Stand with your feet close together and knees soft.
Hinge at your hips and lower your upper body toward your toes.
Reach toward your feet as far as is comfortable.
Return to standing with control and repeat.

summary: A hanging core exercise that raises the feet to touch the bar, demanding strong abdominals, hip flexors, and lats.
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, arms straight and shoulders engaged.
Brace your core and press the bar down slightly with straight arms.
Raise your legs, curling your hips, until your toes touch the bar.
Lower your legs with control back to the hang without swinging.
mistakes: Bending the knees heavily to reach the bar

summary: A gentle standing rotation of the trunk that mobilizes the spine and stretches the obliques and chest.
steps: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and arms crossed or extended in front.
Keep your hips facing forward and slowly rotate your torso to one side.
Pause briefly at a comfortable end range.
Rotate back through center to the other side.
mistakes: Twisting the hips and knees with the torso

summary: A standing rotation that twists the torso side to side with stable hips, working the obliques and mobilizing the spine.
steps: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and knees soft.
Bring your arms up in front of your chest with elbows bent.
Brace your core and rotate your torso to one side, keeping your hips facing forward.
Rotate back through center to the other side in a smooth rhythm.
mistakes: Letting the hips turn with the torso

summary: A dead hang gripping towels draped over a bar that builds forearm and grip strength along with shoulder stability.
steps: Drape two towels over a pull-up bar, one for each hand.
Grip a towel tightly in each hand.
Hang with arms straight and shoulders gently engaged, feet off the floor.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, then lower your feet to the floor.
mistakes: Shoulders fully shrugged toward the ears
Letting the grip slip gradually instead of resetting

summary: A face-down back extension holding a taut towel that strengthens the upper back, lats, and shoulders.
steps: Lie face down holding a towel taut between your hands, arms extended overhead.
Lift your chest and arms a little off the floor, keeping the towel tight.
Pull the towel down behind your head toward your upper back, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Reach the arms back overhead and lower your chest with control.

summary: A bent-over single-arm raise toward a diagonal overhead line that strengthens the lower trapezius and shoulder blade control.
steps: Hinge forward with knees slightly bent and rest one hand on your knee or a bench.
Let the working arm hang, then set that shoulder blade back and down.
Raise the arm up and forward in line with your ear, thumb pointing up.
Lower the arm with control, then switch sides after the set.
mistakes: Twisting the torso to lift higher

summary: A narrow push-up with elbows tucked to the sides that emphasizes the triceps along with the chest and shoulders.
steps: Set up in a high plank with hands directly under your shoulders and your body straight.
Lower your chest toward the floor, keeping your elbows tucked close to your sides.
Let your upper arms travel straight back past your ribs.
Press back up to straight arms.
mistakes: Elbows flaring out to the sides

summary: An advanced suspension rollout that lowers the body by reaching the arms overhead, training the core to resist arching.
steps: Face away from the anchor, hold a handle in each hand, and lean forward with arms straight at chest height.
Brace your core and glutes so your body is straight from head to heels.
Raise your straight arms overhead as your body lowers forward.
Pull your arms back down to chest height to return, keeping the body rigid.
mistakes: Lower back arching at full reach
Bending at the hips on the return
Reaching further than you can control

summary: A suspension row on straps or rings that strengthens the upper back, biceps, and rear shoulders as a lead-up to pull-ups.
steps: Face the anchor holding a handle in each hand and walk your feet forward until your arms are straight and you lean back.
Brace your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Pull your chest to your hands, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are straight.
mistakes: Dropping fast on the way down

summary: A suspension chest fly on straps or rings that strengthens the chest and front of the shoulders through a wide arc.
steps: Set the straps at about mid-chest height and stand facing away from the anchor, a handle in each hand.
Lean forward with arms nearly straight in front of your chest and body in one line from head to heels.
Keep the same elbow bend and open your arms wide as your body lowers forward.
Stop when your hands are about level with your chest, then squeeze your arms back together to return.
mistakes: Bending the elbows into a press
Going past a comfortable shoulder range

summary: A suspension pull to the face with high elbows that strengthens the rear shoulders and upper back.
steps: Set the straps at head to mid-chest height and face the anchor with a handle in each hand.
Walk your feet forward and lean back with arms extended and body straight.
Pull the handles toward your face, driving your elbows high and wide.
Rotate your shoulders so your hands finish beside your temples, then lower back with control.
mistakes: Pulling with the elbows low like a row

summary: A push-up on suspension straps or rings that strengthens the chest and triceps while the unstable handles challenge shoulder control.
steps: Set the handles just above the floor and grip one in each hand.
Get into a plank with arms extended, straps vertical under your shoulders, and body in one line.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest between your hands to a comfortable depth.
Press back up, keeping the handles steady and close to your body.

summary: A suspension raise that lifts the arms into a Y overhead, strengthening the lower trapezius and shoulders.
steps: Set the straps at mid-chest to waist height and face the anchor with a handle in each hand.
Walk your feet forward and lean back with arms extended and body in one line.
With a soft bend in the elbows, raise your arms up and out into a Y overhead.
Lower your arms with control back to the start.
mistakes: Arching the lower back to finish the Y
Bending the elbows into a pull

summary: A support hold with knees tucked to the chest that builds core compression and shoulder strength toward the full L-sit.
steps: Sit with your hands on the floor, parallettes, or parallel bars beside your hips.
Lock your arms and push down to lift your hips off the floor.
Draw your knees toward your chest so your feet hover clear of the ground.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.
mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears
Rounding forward and letting the feet drop

summary: An advanced flowing push-up that rocks back toward the heels and drives forward, building chest, triceps, and shoulder power.
steps: Start in a high plank with hands slightly wider than shoulders.
Lower your chest to just above the floor with elbows tucked about 45 degrees.
As you press up, push your hips back and bend your knees, rocking toward your heels.
Drive forward from the crouch back into the plank to finish the rep.
mistakes: Hips sagging as you drive forward
Elbows flaring wide at the bottom

summary: A single-leg hip thrust with the upper back on a bench that strongly targets the glutes and builds hip stability.
steps: Sit with your upper back against a sturdy bench and one foot flat on the floor, the other leg lifted.
Brace your core and tuck your chin slightly.
Drive through the heel to lift your hips until your thigh and torso are in a straight line.
Lower your hips with control, then switch sides after the set.
mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top
Pelvis dropping toward the free leg

summary: A lunge performed on one leg at a time that strengthens the glutes and quadriceps with continuous tension.
steps: Stand tall with hands on your hips and step one foot forward into a split stance.
Lower your back knee toward the floor, keeping your torso upright.
Press through the front foot to rise without locking out or pausing.
Keep moving smoothly on the same leg, then switch sides.
mistakes: Bouncing the back knee off the floor

summary: A push-up from an inverted-V position that shifts load to the shoulders and triceps, building overhead pressing strength.
steps: Start in a plank, then walk your feet in and lift your hips high into an inverted V.
Place your hands about shoulder-width apart with your head between your arms.
Bend your elbows to lower the top of your head toward the floor just in front of your hands.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
mistakes: Hips dropping into a regular push-up

summary: A face-down shoulder raise with the arms bent in a W shape that strengthens the mid and lower trapezius and rotator cuff.
steps: Lie face down with your forehead on a towel and elbows bent, arms forming a W beside your body.
Draw your shoulder blades back and down.
Lift your arms off the floor, turning your thumbs toward the ceiling.
Pause briefly, then lower with control.

summary: A glute bridge that walks the feet out and back in small steps, training the glutes and hamstrings with core control.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, and arms by your sides.
Squeeze your glutes and lift your hips into a bridge.
Keeping your hips high, take small steps to walk your feet away from you.
Walk your feet back in, then lower your hips with control.
mistakes: Hips dropping as the feet walk out

summary: A gentle wrist mobility drill on all fours that rocks the body forward and back over planted hands.
steps: Start on hands and knees with palms flat, hands under your shoulders.
Slowly rock forward so your shoulders move past your wrists.
Rock back toward your heels, keeping your palms planted.
Move smoothly within a comfortable, pain-free range.
mistakes: Lifting the heels of the hands

summary: A gentle forearm stretch that draws the fingers back with the arm straight, easing the wrist flexors.
steps: Extend one arm in front of you at shoulder height with the palm facing away and fingers pointing down.
Hold the fingers with your other hand.
Gently draw the fingers back toward you until you feel a stretch in the forearm.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.
